messages.subject: Questions about within_module_deg_z_score : "Error in vapply"
parts:
Dear Chris Watson,

First of all, thank you very very much for such a helpful package.
I'm calculating some network indicators using your package, and I had a trouble with errors when calculating within module degrees.

This is codes I wrote :

### Preparations
library(braingGraph)
graph<-read.graph("graph1.gml", format="gml")
member<-as.matrix(read.csv("member.csv"))
member1<-as.matrix(member[,2])

###Calculation
within_module_deg_z_score(graph,member1)


And I got this :
Error in vapply(vs, function(x) degree(comms[[memb[x]]])[V(g)$name[x]],  :
  values must be length 1,
 but FUN(X[[1]]) result is length 0


I could calculate participation coefficients with my data set.
I'd appreciate any help or advice.

Thank you.

messages.author: 28bb28f8fe8898a5
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Questions about within_module_deg_z_score : "Error in vapply"
parts:
Hello,

The second argument to that function should be a vector (although I think what you use as the input should have worked), so I recommend that you first try changing your 4th line of code to be:
member1 <- member[, 2]

or skipping that line and just typing:
within_module_deg_z_score(graph, member[, 2])

If that still doesn't work, you can send me the graph and csv files and I can take a look.

Chris

messages.author: 28bb28f8fe8898a5
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Questions about within_module_deg_z_score : "Error in vapply"
parts:
Hi,
The problem is that your data are zero-indexed, whereas R is 1-indexed. Additionally, the function looks for a vertex attribute called "name". So the following code will work:

graph <- read.graph('graph1.gml', format='gml')
member <- read.csv('member.csv')
V(graph)$name <- V(graph)$id + 1
member1 <- member[, 2] + 1
z <- within_module_deg_z_score(graph, member1)

Since you have a large graph, you can speed this up if you like. To edit the function, you would first type:
within_module_deg_z_score <- edit(within_module_deg_z_score)

And then edit the appropriate line with the following code: (I have 6 CPU cores so in using the following code total processing time was reduced to 42sec from 197sec)
Ki[vs] <- plyr::aaply(vs, .margins=1, function(x) degree(comms[[member1[x]]])[V(graph)$name[x]], .parallel=T)

You need to have the "plyr" package installed, which should have been installed when you install "brainGraph".

Let me know if you have any other questions,
Chris
